newsitem.title: USA: Higher oil prices to fuel increase in US drilling.
newsitem.headline: Higher oil prices to fuel increase in US drilling.

text.p: Higher oil and natural gas prices will fuel a 9.2 percent increase in the number of oil and natural gas wells drilled in the United States, an industry trade magazine forecast on Friday.
World Oil magazine editors forecast 25,719 domestic wells will be drilled this year, including 1,100 wells in the offshore Gulf of Mexico and 8,590 in Texas.
"The rub is, you probably couldn't drill more wells (in the U.S. Gulf) if you had to, because you couldn't find any rigs," World Oil editor Bob Snyder said.

Excluding the United States, an estimated 37,122 wells will be drilled this year, with drilling activity on the rise in Russia but falling off by as much as 10.5 percent in Canada, the magazine editors said in their annual forecast.

The increased drilling comes as world oil supplies of 70.9 million barrels per day (mmbpd) were outstripped by demand of 71.6 mmbpd, a 2.0 percent increase on the year. Domestic demand rose 3.6 percent to 19.1 mmbpd, outpacing U.S. production of 6.4 mmbpd, which was down 1.7 percent on the year, the editors said in a presentation in Houston.
